message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look at the Canadian long weekends in **2023** (i.e., holidays that fall on a Friday or Monday, giving you a 3‑ or 4‑day break).  
(If you’re in a province that observes a different holiday—e.g., Family Day in BC is on March 20—you’ll need to adjust accordingly.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Weekend Days Included |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Good Friday** | April 7 | Friday | Fri‑Sun (Apr 7‑9) |
| **Family Day** (Ontario, Alberta, etc.) | February 20 | Monday | Fri‑Mon (Feb 17‑20) |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 | Monday | Fri‑Mon (May 19‑22) |
| **Labour Day** | September 4 | Monday | Fri‑Mon (Sep 1‑4) |
| **Thanksgiving** | October 9 | Monday | Fri‑Mon (Oct 6‑9) |
| **Christmas** | December 25 | Monday | Fri‑Mon (Dec 22‑25) |

> **Notes**  
> • If you’re in a province where Family Day falls on a different date (e.g., BC: March 20, 2023), replace the date above with the local one.  
> • Canada Day (July 1, Saturday) and Boxing Day (Dec 26, Tuesday) do not create automatic long weekends, but you can still take adjacent weekdays off for a 3‑day break.  

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app!
